title: Porsche / BMW Luxury Care & Cost Control
subtitle: OEM fluid approvals, electronics gremlins, and indie-specialist strategies — keep the badge happy without burning the budget.

prerequisites: Owner's manual oil/fluid approval codes (LL-01, MB, Porsche A40, etc.)
OBD tool capable of reading manufacturer modules when possible
Budget for specialist labor on electronics and brakes
parts_checklist: AGM battery if equipped (registration may be required)

adaptive_rules.coach_note: BMW: match Longlife oil approvals, watch for oil filter housing gasket seepage, and plan battery registration after 12V swaps.
adaptive_rules.oil_spec_hint: BMW Longlife approval on the jug — viscosity alone is not enough.

adaptive_rules.coach_note: Porsche: A40 / C40 (and model-specific) approvals matter. PDK/coolant services and IMS-era concerns belong with a Porsche indie or dealer.
adaptive_rules.oil_spec_hint: Confirm Porsche oil approval for your exact engine/year.

adaptive_rules.coach_note: Euro electronics often store faults across modules — a generic code reader can miss the real story.
Past 80k on these brands: budget cooling components, mounts, and carbon cleaning conversations with a specialist.

risk_confirm.title: Advanced electronics diagnosis risk
risk_confirm.body: Clearing codes without fixing root causes can hide safety faults (ABS, airbag, stability). Do not clear airbag/ABS lights to 'make them go away.' When module access is unclear, find a nearby specialist shop.

risk_confirm.title: Luxury 12V / IBS service risk
risk_confirm.body: Incorrect battery type or skipped registration can damage the charging system. High-voltage hybrids (if equipped) have orange cables that must not be touched. When unsure, find a nearby shop.
